newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian court rejects evidence in Ogoni plea.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian court rejects evidence in Ogoni plea.

text.p: A Nigerian court has rejected a plea by 19 Ogonis that they should be released from prison because of torture and starvation since their arrest on murder charges in the same case as hanged author Ken Saro-Wiwa.

Human rights lawyer Olisa Agbakoba told Reuters the judge in the eastern city of Port Harcourt said the evidence presented on Tuesday was indirect and could not be used to support the claim that the 19 should be released.
"We will be filing a new plea for review today," he said.
The Ogonis were charged in May 1995 with complicity in the murder of four prominent pro-government chiefs in their volatile oil-producing homeland.

The detainees have complained of torture and starvation, and of having to spend long periods locked in manacles. They also say they are not allowed medical treatment for chronic health problems they have developed in detention.
The execution of nine Ogoni activists, including Saro-Wiwa, in November 1995 for the same murders brought worldwide condemnation of Nigeria's military leaders.
